claims.claim: The Model for Improvement was developed by Associates in Process Improvement and is built around three questions: what are we trying to accomplish, how will we know that a change is an improvement, and what change can we make that will result in improvement.

The PDSA (Plan-Do-Study-Act) cycle tests a change on a small scale in the real-world setting by planning it, trying it, observing the results, and acting on what is learned; teams run multiple cycles before full implementation.

PDSA descends from Walter Shewhart's 1939 specification-production-inspection cycle and W. Edwards Deming's 1950 cycle; the Japanese PDCA form appeared in 1951, and Deming later named the Plan-Do-Study-Act version, preferring 'Study' over 'Check'.

Lean, sometimes called the Toyota Production System, focuses on cutting wasteful steps so that only value-adding activity remains, and uses value stream mapping to visualize each step in the flow of care.

Six Sigma aims to eliminate defects and reduce variation using the DMAIC roadmap (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control); a six-sigma process is one in which 99.99966% of production opportunities are expected to be free of defects.

Common-cause variation is inherent in a process, while special-cause variation is due to an attributable cause; Shewhart (control) charts display data over time with upper and lower control limits and are the way to distinguish the two.
A run chart plots data over time against the median; a shift signaling non-random change is six or more consecutive points all above or all below the median, with points on the median skipped.
A central-line infection rate falling from 12 infections per 4,000 line-days (3.00 per 1,000) to 5 per 4,500 line-days (1.11 per 1,000) is a 63% relative reduction.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The threshold for a 'shift' in time-series data
positions: Run-chart rules use six or more consecutive points on one side of the median (eight if 20+ data points)
Control-chart practice commonly uses eight consecutive points on one side of the centerline
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses the IHI run-chart rule (six points) and notes that control-chart conventions differ, so the two tools are described separately.
The lesson uses PDSA (the healthcare-standard term) and explains PDCA as the closely related industrial form with shared Shewhart-Deming roots.
